$comment: U16: push U2 (W25Q512JV NOR flash) 1.000 mm east to open the crystal lane.
DISPLACEMENT IS CONSTRAINED TO A BAND, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE DESIGN INPUT.
/GND stitching vias sit at x = 169.565 and do not move. U2's west pad column
moves to 167.590 + dx, so legal clearance requires dx <= 1.075 OR dx >= 2.875.
A first attempt at 2.500 mm landed inside that forbidden band and produced 33
violations -- pads on stitching vias, the exposed pad over /+3V3, /+5V shorting
IO1. Anything in 1.075 < dx < 2.875 collides by construction.
1.000 mm is the low-churn choice: it clears every existing via and track with no
collateral, and still takes the U2-to-X1 courtyard gap from 0.86 to 1.86 mm --
roughly double the 0.96 mm lane that the crystal guard and the QSPI escape vias
were competing for, which is what forced both walk-backs in kicad_netclass.json.
Going to >= 2.875 mm would need 31 segments of /GND, /+3V3, /+5V and /CS_R ripped
and re-routed through the flash's neighbourhood; that buys 2 mm more lane for a
great deal more risk, and /CS_R is already the net plan 002 wants left alone.
WHY THIS IS ELECTRICALLY FREE. Plan 002 measured the QSPI budget: at 100 MHz SDR
the window is tCK/2 = 5000 ps and a 10% skew allocation is 500 ps ~ 77 mm.
Translating U2 moves every pad equally, so added length is COMMON MODE, not skew
-- skew moves 22 um across 7 mm of travel. 1 mm costs ~6.5 ps of flight time on
CLK and data alike, shifting the sampling window rather than eating it.
WHY NOT ROTATE. All four orientations evaluated: 180 deg (current) is best at
63.15 mm total; 0 deg 70.22, 90 deg 69.60, 270 deg 69.35, and both quarter-turns
fail courtyard clearance. The 8 mm column split is fixed by the WSON package and
180 deg already faces 3 of 5 signals (IO0, CLK, IO3) toward U1.
WHY NOT REMAP IN FIRMWARE. QUADSPI BK1_IO2 has exactly two alternates on this
package, PF7 (pin 21) and PE2 (pin 1), and BOTH are on the east edge. IO0/IO1/IO3
could move to PD11/PD12/PD13 on the west side but IO2 cannot follow, splitting a
parallel bus across opposite sides of the package. No firmware change helps.
METHOD: TRANSLATE, DO NOT RE-AUTHOR. Every U2-side via and stub moves exactly
+1.000 mm and its feeding run extends by the same 1.000 mm, so existing clearances
are preserved by construction rather than re-derived.
ALL EIGHT SIGNAL PADS ARE HANDLED. The first draft rerouted only IO0-3 and CLK and
left /QSPI_NCS behind, shorting to the exposed pad. NCS is in the held qspi group
so it is hand-routed here too. Pads 4 (/GND) and 8 (/+3V3) reach the pours and need
no track work.
U2 pad 9 is a 4.65 x 5.20 mm /GND thermal land; after the move it spans
x 170.265-174.915, y 104.606-109.806. No QSPI top copper in this spec enters it.
VERIFY AFTER APPLYING: kicad_measure --against (only the six QSPI nets and U2
should differ), and analyze_pcb.py --full --compact asserting zero VP-001 -- the
QSPI walk-back was six escape vias inside U2's pads and DRC never said a word.
REVISION 2. Only IO1 and NCS move their vias -- their old ones (174.405, 174.454)
fall INSIDE the enlarged exposed pad after the move and must clear it. IO0, CLK and
IO3 keep their vias where they are and extend only the top-layer stub to the pad.
Moving those three created new via-to-via conflicts and one via-in-pad (VP-001 went
1 -> 2), and extending IO3 on the BOTTOM layer put it 0.091 mm from IO1's existing
bottom run at y=107.750 -- a direct short. The top layer west of the pads is free
because U2's old pad column vacated it, so the stubs go there instead.
/+3V3's diagonal now crosses U2 pad 4, so it is ripped here and left for the router;
+3V3 is not in the held set.
REVISION 3 -- FULL CLEARANCE AT +2.500 mm. Threading around the existing copper was
tried at three displacements and failed three different ways, so the destination is
cleared instead: /GND, /+3V3 and /+5V are ripped inside x 169.0-179.2, y 103.6-110.8
and re-established by tools/kicad_route.py afterwards -- none of them is held.
/CS_R runs at y=103.496, outside that window, and is deliberately left alone.
With the blocking copper gone the displacement band no longer applies, so this takes
+2.500 mm: the knee of the original sweep, where the U2-to-X1 gap reaches 3.36 mm
(3.5x the contested lane) and bus coverage over solid Inner1 GND peaks at 86%.
